About This Job
We are looking for people with kind, compassionate hearts who want to make a true difference to the quality of life for our clients to join our team in Burnley as a Live In Care Professional.
As a Live-In Care Professional, you will reside in a client’s home, providing non-medical support to help them maintain independence and comfort in their own environment.
Primary Responsibilities;
• Provide live in care, usually working alone
• Reflect the core values of Home Instead franchise
• Contribute to a positive living environment to enhance a client’s quality of life
• As you will be staying in the client’s home, you will follow their house rules and be mindful of their need for privacy
• You may be the only person the client sees over a period of time, it is therefore essential to document daily activities and report any changes or causes for concern in a client’s needs or living conditions
• You need to be clear about when to seek help and advice to keep clients safe and promote their well-being
• Provide personalised support and companionship to clients
• Assist with daily activities to enhance quality of life
This role is perfect for someone who values making a meaningful difference, enjoys companionship, and takes pride in delivering excellent care.

Qualifications
You do not need any experience or particular qualifications to become a Care Professional. However, it would be useful to have some experience of working in a care setting or interacting with older people. This could be personal experience of caring for a family member or voluntary experience. You will have a passion for supporting others and pride yourself on delivering an outstanding service. You will be reliable, trustworthy and respectful. You will enjoy building professional friendships and comfortable in spending time in the company of others.

Additional Information
As a Live In Care Professional, you will be provided with 3 meals a day or an allowance from the client, a separate room to stay and access to a TV and WiFi.  In addition, we offer comprehensive training and support.
If you're looking for work which is extremely rewarding and satisfactory and have a high-degree of  flexibility to meet our clients' needs, we would love to hear from you. Please contact us on 01282 911 300
This role is subject to Right To Work In the UK & a DBS enhanced disclosure.

About This Job
Head Housekeeper
The Croft – Amersham - Buckinghamshire
Salary: £9.21ph
Hours: 25 hours per week
The Croft is a modern purpose-built registered care home in Amersham with specially designed accommodation for up to 64 older people. All rooms are en-suite and can be personalised with people’s own effects to create a real home-from-home environment.
Accommodation is arranged in four self-contained living areas all of which are comfortably and attractively furnished. The Croft provides person centred care and support to older people and to those living with dementia.
Our team are able to support residents to live as independent a life as any health condition will allow.
Head of housekeeping Job Purpose:
To lead the team of Housekeeping staff, including laundry assistants, to ensure that the service is clean, tidy and maintained to the highest standards of cleanliness and hygiene – Promoting home from home.
Main Responsibilities:
• Take the lead in supervising the housekeeping team in their roles and required duties
• Ensure that the highest standards of cleanliness are met within the service
• Consult with residents on a regular basis such as attending suite meetings, to ensure that their needs and choices in relation to housekeeping and laundry are being met.
• Ensure that all housekeeping and laundry consumables are ordered from nominated suppliers
• Ensure that stock takes are carried out each week
• Implement, monitor and maintain cleaning schedules for the service and ensure that they are adhered to
• Ensure that supplies are stored safely and used effectively to minimise wastage
• Maintain a high standard of hygiene within the service
• Adhere to and promote COSHH guidelines
• Attend relatives and residents meeting whenever possible
• Monitor staff training requirements; working with the deputy manager to arrange training
• Carry out housekeeping audits
• Report any maintenance issues to the administrator for onward reporting
• Work alongside the housekeeping team, demonstrating and promoting best practice
• Development and monitoring of the induction and supervision process
• Supporting new staff through the induction process
Experience: Housekeeping: 1 year (Preferred)

About This Job
We’re looking for Care Professionals who are kind and compassionate and who, by understanding our values and our mission, are dedicated to delivering the highest standard of care. To ensure continuity for both Clients and Care Professionals, you will see the same Clients every week, with minimum one hour visits, enabling you to build a relationship and a routine focused around quality of life in the comfort of the Client’s home.
Home Care is care carried out in an older adult’s own home, rather than in another setting like a hospital, assisted living facility, care home or nursing home. If the person needs specific medical care it may be recommended that they move to one of these facilities, but most types of care – including complex care, dementia care, palliative care and more – can take place in the home. Home carers can assist with daily living activities in a safe manner while the older person remains in the comfort and familiarity of their own home where they can retain some or most of their independence. Home carers can help with tasks such as:
• Personal care (such as getting to the bathroom and getting dressed)
• Helping clients get to the bathroom during the night
• Providing medication reminders, and administering this if relevant
• Encouraging the person to eat nutritious meals
• Providing meal preparation and cooking, while adhering to any dietary requirements
• Helping with regular housework and other chores
• Helping clients with mobility issues to move around safely in the home
• Driving clients to weekly appointments
• Offering regular companionship and observing their mental health
• Organising enjoyable and stimulating activities for the client
The home environment is a key part of maintaining dignity in care for older adults, more so than other settings. Studies have found those receiving care in other settings, such as a hospital, experienced mild to severe loss of dignity. For this reason, helping an older adult to remain in their own home could drastically improve their care experience.

Qualifications
There’s nothing more powerful than the ability to change somebody’s life for the better every day, whether that’s simply keeping them company, or offering more advanced personal or dementia care. And we’ll give you all the training you need to confidently make the role your own. As a Care Professional, you can make a world of difference to people’s lives the minute you step through your client’s door, helping them to live independently, at home, with exceptional care. So if you just can’t help but care, you’ll find your role at Home Instead.

Additional Information
Our motto is ‘To us its Personal’ and we live up to this statement every day both in the way we treat our clients and our Care Professionals. As we provide relationship-led care, we match our Care Professionals to clients based on a range of factors including; personalities, interests and hobbies. Along with this we focus on continuity for both client and Care Profesional which means we can create meaningful relationships between Care Professionals and their clients, which makes their jobs even more fulfilling.
In addition to careful client matching, all visits are a minimum of one hour long, so there is plenty of time to provide high quality care and spend time with the client. When you join the Home Instead family you have the best of both worlds – all the benefits of a small, community-based business, but backed with over 25 years of global expertise in providing exceptional home care.

About This Job
We’re looking for a Payments Architect to join our growing team in London. This is a senior architectural leadership role with deep payments specialism, shaping and delivering enterprise-grade payment platforms from gateway and authorisation layers through to clearing, settlement and financial management.
You’ll bring strong payments domain expertise, but you won’t be boxed into payments-only work. You’re a well-rounded architect who can apply the same rigour to wider platform and enterprise challenges, flexing across domains as client priorities shift. That might mean moving from payments architecture into broader solution leadership, integration strategy, cloud platform decisions or security and identity-driven programmes.
This role suits someone who thrives in complex environments and operates confidently at the intersection of business strategy and technical execution. You’ll engage across the full lifecycle, from early discovery and architectural shaping through to delivery oversight, ensuring solutions are scalable, secure, commercially viable and aligned to long-term platform strategy.
In addition to payments architecture, you’ll play a key role in unifying user experience across multiple portals. You’ll drive integration strategies that deliver seamless and consistent customer journeys, supported by robust identity and access management capabilities.
What you’ll be doing
You’ll bring expertise in merchant acquiring and payment processing across both online and physical acceptance channels. This includes understanding gateway architecture, authorisation lifecycles, 3-D Secure (3DS) and Strong Customer Authentication (SCA), scheme integrations, tokenisation, fraud decisioning, reconciliation and settlement.
You’ll also contribute to shaping integrated digital experiences, ensuring multiple user portals and systems are unified into a coherent, secure and scalable user experience supported by modern identity solutions.

Qualifications
• Design and review scalable, resilient payment architectures capable of supporting high transaction volumes and demanding availability requirements
• Define and govern non-functional requirements including latency, throughput, availability, recoverability, observability and security
• Shape API strategies, integration models and event-driven or distributed system designs that support extensibility and regulatory compliance
• Architect and implement Single Sign-On (SSO) and distributed identity solutions across platforms
• Integrate enterprise systems with Identity Providers (IdPs), with preference for FIS Infinity IdP
• Contribute to and support the configuration, maintenance and troubleshooting of IAM platforms
• Ensure secure authentication, authorisation and identity federation across systems
• Drive strategies to unify user portals and deliver seamless cross-platform user experiences
• Contribute to PCI DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard) scoping strategies and secure-by-design approaches within cloud and hybrid environments
• Participate in architectural governance forums, representing Endava with clarity and authority
• Support pre-sales and bid shaping activities by defining credible, commercially grounded target-state solutions
• Translate architectural decisions into clear executive narratives, articulating trade-offs, risks and investment implications
• Flex across wider architecture responsibilities beyond payments when needed, applying strong architectural fundamentals to adjacent domains and evolving programmes
Where appropriate, you will explore the application of emerging capabilities, including AI-driven optimisation, intelligent routing, fraud modelling and AIOps, ensuring innovation is grounded in practical, value-led use cases.
How you’ll work
You’ll be comfortable speaking the language of enterprise, solution and data architects, and equally confident engaging in detailed technical discussions with engineering teams or strategic conversations with business stakeholders. You’ll bring depth where it matters most, while staying adaptable as delivery needs change.

Additional Information

• Finance: Competitive salary package, share plan, company performance bonuses, value-based recognition awards, referral bonus;
• Career Development: Career coaching, global career opportunities, non-linear career paths, internal development programmes for management and technical leadership;
• Learning Opportunities: Complex projects, rotations, internal tech communities, training, certifications, coaching, online learning platforms subscriptions, pass-it-on sessions, workshops, conferences;

About This Job

About the Role
At Wise, our Staff Analyst is one of our most senior individual contributor roles in Analytics.
A Staff-level Analyst at Wise is a senior IC who defines and owns the analytical direction for a broad problem space or domain — identifying the right problems to solve, shaping priorities and ways of working, setting the measurement approach, building scalable solutions, and influencing senior stakeholders to drive outcomes across multiple teams.
In this role, you'll own the analytical direction for sustainability and pricing across Global Product. You'll help us understand the underlying economics of our products, how costs and revenues are generated and allocated, and whether we're building a business that can sustain its growth over the long term.
You'll work closely with Product, Finance, Commercial, Engineering and other teams to bring a much clearer understanding of the economics behind our growth. This includes informing how we allocate costs and revenue across products, markets and customer behaviours, and translating those insights into better pricing decisions.
As Wise continues to evolve from a cross-border product into a broader account offering, you'll play an important role in ensuring our pricing remains competitive and attractive to customers while supporting our ambition for sustainable growth and strong contribution margins.
This is a role for someone who can combine deep commercial and analytical thinking with strong technical capability — setting direction while remaining hands-on in the work.
What you'll do
•
Own the analytical direction for sustainability and pricing across Global Product, defining the key questions, priorities and analytical approaches needed to understand the economics of our business.
•
Build a clear view of our unit economics, developing robust approaches to understanding how costs and revenues are generated across products, customer segments, markets and behaviours.
•
Shape our cost and revenue allocation frameworks, ensuring we have a consistent and meaningful understanding of the economics of different products, customer journeys and revenue streams.
•
Monitor the sustainability of our growth, identifying where growth is creating or diluting contribution margin, understanding the underlying drivers and highlighting emerging risks and opportunities.
•
Inform cross-border pricing decisions, helping us understand the relationship between pricing, customer attractiveness, competitiveness, conversion, retention and long-term value.
•
Shape product pricing across the Wise Account, identifying opportunities to improve how we price different products, features and services while maintaining a compelling customer proposition.
•
Connect pricing and profitability decisions, ensuring we understand the trade-offs between customer growth, product adoption, revenue generation and contribution margin.
•
Partner with senior stakeholders across Product, Finance and Commercial to translate complex economic analysis into clear recommendations and influence strategic decisions.
•
Lead large, complex analytical initiatives from problem definition through to measurable business impact.
•
Build scalable data models, frameworks and monitoring solutions that improve how we understand and manage the economics of Global Product.
•
Champion technical excellence in SQL, data modelling and analytical problem-solving, while mentoring other Analysts and raising the analytical bar across Wise.
What you'll bring
•
Commercial and strategic thinking — you understand what drives a sustainable business and can connect detailed economic analysis to wider commercial and product strategy.
•
Strong unit economics expertise — you've worked with complex cost, revenue, profitability and contribution margin models and understand the challenges of allocating economics across products, customers and markets.
•
Pricing expertise — you understand pricing strategy, customer price sensitivity, competitive positioning and the trade-offs between growth, monetisation and profitability.
•
Best-in-class technical capability — expert SQL, strong data modelling skills and a track record of personally delivering complex analytical work.
•
Cross-functional partnership — you've worked closely with Product, Finance, Commercial and other functions, shaping decisions rather than operating as a downstream reporting function.
•
Senior stakeholder influence — you're comfortable challenging assumptions, translating complex analysis into clear recommendations and influencing senior leaders.
•
High autonomy — you create clarity where there is ambiguity, proactively identify opportunities and don't need a neatly defined problem handed to you.
•
Strong product and customer judgement — you understand the impact pricing and commercial decisions have on customer behaviour, product adoption and long-term value.
•
Technical leadership without people management — you lead through expertise, standards, frameworks, mentoring and the quality of your own delivery.

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/wise/7440001459.description_excerpt:
About This Job
About The Team
The Global KYC and Onboarding squad works to make onboarding into Wise safe, compliant, efficient, and scalable. Within that squad, Wise Platform Verification focuses on verification for Wise Platform partners and their customers.
Wise Platform Verification supports customers who access Wise through our partners. The domain spans different partner models, markets and operational routes. Parts of it are still difficult to measure and rely on fragmented or manual processes. This role will help the team build a reliable view of performance, identify the highest-value problems and establish better ways of working. When these flows are unclear or manual, partners can face delays, customers can hit avoidable friction, operations teams carry unnecessary work, and controls become harder to audit.
The team is building a more scalable verification model for Wise Platform: explicit requirements, better control monitoring, clearer operational flows, stronger automation, and partner-ready processes that can grow with Wise Platform.
About The Role
We are looking for an Implementation Manager to bring analytical rigour and process discipline to Wise Platform Verification. You will use data to understand how verification works across partners, identify the biggest sources of friction and operational cost, and lead improvements from diagnosis through implementation and measurement.
Your mission is to turn complex partner-verification problems into measurable implementation plans, trusted metrics, clear operating models, repeatable rollout playbooks, and automation opportunities. You will work across Product, Engineering, Analytics, Product Compliance, Risk, Partner Due Diligence and Operations teams, regional teams, and partner-facing teams to make sure verification changes launch safely, work operationally, and are measured after release.
This is not a coordinator-only role. You will create structure where it does not exist yet: map processes, define KPIs, identify root causes, challenge data quality, build launch scorecards, design operating cadences, and help move manual workflows toward automation.
What you will own
•
Map Wise Platform verification processes end to end, including partner models, control triggers, evidence flows, operational routing, RFIs, exceptions, and recovery paths.
•
Identify process and automation opportunities that reduce manual review, avoidable partner RFIs, misrouting, operational rework, and partner/customer disruption.
•
Define implementation plans for high-priority verification changes, including scope, owners, milestones, risks, launch gates, runbooks, training, adoption, monitoring, and escalation paths.
•
Build trusted KPI definitions, dashboards, launch scorecards, and weekly/monthly performance narratives that help the team make decisions.
•
Partner with Analytics and Data Science to validate data quality, segment impact, size populations, measure outcomes, and distinguish true performance changes from reporting or process artifacts.
•
Partner with Engineering to turn operational needs into implementable requirements while understanding technical constraints, dependencies, rollout paths, and migration risks.
•
Partner with Product Compliance, Risk, and Ops to make sure process changes meet control objectives, remain auditable, and work for the teams reviewing cases.
•
Support automation and process migration work, including moving fragile manual processes and legacy workflows toward scalable product or platform patterns.
•
Lead root-cause analysis for operational issues and partner-impacting verification pain points, then track fixes to closure and prevent recurrence through standards, monitoring, and documentation.
What success looks like in the first 6-12 months:
•
WPV has clearer process maps and ownership for the highest-impact partner verification workflows.
•
High-priority process changes launch with implementation plans, metrics, launch gates, runbooks, monitoring, and adoption tracking.
•
Manual review and partner RFI pain points are sized, prioritised, and converted into a practical automation or process-improvement backlog.
•
Partner Due Diligence, Operations, and partner-facing teams have clearer routing, context, escalation paths, and feedback loops.
•
The team can trust its core operating metrics and use them for prioritisation, launch readiness, and post-launch learning.
•
Operational incidents and recurring process issues lead to documented root causes, owners, fixes, and prevention mechanisms.
•
Legacy process or service ownership issues are mapped and sequenced with clear migration or handover plans.
This role gives you the opportunity to:
•
Work on one of the most important scaling problems for Wise Platform.
•
Build the operating system for partner verification across product, engineering, compliance, risk, data, and operations.
•
Improve how partners and their customers move through verification, while keeping controls robust and auditable.
•
Turn manual and fragmented workflows into measurable, repeatable, automatable processes.
•
Become an expert in partner verification, operational automation, risk controls, and platform-scale implementation.

Additional Information
• ​​​​​​Base salary: £90,000 - £130,000 gross/year (based on experience & interview outcomes)
•
Restricted Stock Units (RSUs)
•
Numerous other benefits
For everyone, everywhere. We're people building money without borders  — without judgement or prejudice, too. We believe teams are strongest when they are diverse, equitable and inclusive.
We're proud to have a truly international team, and we celebrate our differences.
Inclusive teams help us live our values and make sure every Wiser feels respected, empowered to contribute towards our mission and able to progress in their careers.
If you want to find out more about what it's like to work at Wise visit Wise.Jobs.

About This Job
We are looking for an experienced analytical scientist to join our Innovation team at LGC Assure in Fordham. This is a hands-on role focused on independently developing, optimising and validating analytical methods using LC-MS, troubleshooting complex analytical challenges and developing new testing solutions to support our specialist laboratories.
Working across different areas of the business, you will take ownership of method development projects from initial investigation through to validation and implementation. You'll need strong practical LC-MS expertise, a structured approach to problem-solving and the ability to deliver robust analytical solutions within a busy commercial testing environment, balancing multiple projects and deadlines.
If you enjoy solving complex analytical problems, developing new approaches and working collaboratively to turn scientific challenges into practical solutions, this could be an excellent opportunity to make a direct impact on our scientific capabilities.
What you'll be doing
•
Independently develop, optimise and validate analytical methods using LC-MS, taking ownership of projects from initial feasibility and method development through to validation and implementation.
•
Troubleshoot complex analytical challenges, identifying root causes and developing practical solutions to improve method performance and analytical reliability.
•
Develop and optimise extraction methods and sample preparation workflows to meet different sample matrix and testing requirements.
•
Configure, operate and optimise LC-MS instrumentation to generate reliable, high-quality analytical data.
•
Analyse and interpret complex scientific data, identifying trends, investigating issues and supporting evidence-based decisions.
•
Support innovation projects across the business, working with laboratory teams to develop new testing capabilities and improve existing methods.
•
Manage multiple projects and competing priorities, delivering high-quality outputs within agreed timelines.
•
Produce clear scientific documentation, including technical reports, validation summaries, standard operating procedures and project updates.
•
Present scientific findings and project outcomes confidently to internal teams and external customers.
•
Support customer discussions by explaining analytical approaches, providing scientific insight and contributing to technical solutions.
•
Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that enhance laboratory processes, analytical methods and ways of working.
•
Maintain accurate records and ensure work is completed in accordance with ISO 17025 requirements and applicable quality standards.

Qualifications
You are an experienced analytical scientist with strong practical LC-MS expertise and a track record of developing and improving analytical methods. You're comfortable taking ownership of scientific challenges, investigating problems independently and working with colleagues across different disciplines to deliver effective solutions.
You enjoy working in a fast-paced laboratory environment where scientific quality, customer requirements and delivery deadlines are equally important.
You will have:
•
A degree in Chemistry or a relevant scientific discipline.
•
Significant, recent hands-on experience using LC-MS instrumentation in an analytical laboratory.
•
Demonstrable experience independently developing, optimising and validating analytical methods, rather than solely operating established methods or providing instrument support.

Practical experience troubleshooting analytical methods and instrumentation, identifying root causes and implementing solutions.

Experience developing extraction methods and sample preparation workflows.
•
Experience working in a busy analytical laboratory, ideally within commercial testing, contract testing or a similarly delivery-focused environment.

The ability to interpret complex analytical data and communicate scientific findings clearly.

Strong organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects, prioritise competing demands and deliver to deadlines.

Excellent written communication skills, including experience producing technical reports and scientific documentation.

Confidence presenting scientific information to a range of audiences, both internally and externally.

A collaborative approach, with the ability to work effectively as part of a team while independently managing your own workload.

Knowledge of ISO 17025 accreditation standards and laboratory quality systems.

About This Job
We’re looking for Care Professionals who are kind and compassionate and who, by understanding our values and our mission, are dedicated to delivering the highest standard of care. To ensure continuity for both Clients and Care Professionals, you will see the same Clients every week, with minimum one hour visits, enabling you to build a relationship and a routine focused around quality of life in the comfort of the Client’s home.
Home Care is care carried out in an older adult’s own home, rather than in another setting like a hospital, assisted living facility, care home or nursing home. If the person needs specific medical care it may be recommended that they move to one of these facilities, but most types of care – including complex care, dementia care, palliative care and more – can take place in the home. Home carers can assist with daily living activities in a safe manner while the older person remains in the comfort and familiarity of their own home where they can retain some or most of their independence. Home carers can help with tasks such as:
• Personal care (such as getting to the bathroom and getting dressed)
• Helping clients get to the bathroom during the night
• Providing medication reminders, and administering this if relevant
• Encouraging the person to eat nutritious meals
• Providing meal preparation and cooking, while adhering to any dietary requirements
• Helping with regular housework and other chores
• Helping clients with mobility issues to move around safely in the home
• Driving clients to weekly appointments
• Offering regular companionship and observing their mental health
• Organising enjoyable and stimulating activities for the client
The home environment is a key part of maintaining dignity in care for older adults, more so than other settings. Studies have found those receiving care in other settings, such as a hospital, experienced mild to severe loss of dignity. For this reason, helping an older adult to remain in their own home could drastically improve their care experience.

Qualifications
There’s nothing more powerful than the ability to change somebody’s life for the better every day, whether that’s simply keeping them company, or offering more advanced personal or dementia care. And we’ll give you all the training you need to confidently make the role your own. As a Care Professional, you can make a world of difference to people’s lives the minute you step through your client’s door, helping them to live independently, at home, with exceptional care. So if you just can’t help but care, you’ll find your role at Home Instead.

Additional Information
Our motto is ‘To us its Personal’ and we live up to this statement every day both in the way we treat our clients and our Care Professionals. As we provide relationship-led care, we match our Care Professionals to clients based on a range of factors including; personalities, interests and hobbies. Along with this we focus on continuity for both client and Care Profesional which means we can create meaningful relationships between Care Professionals and their clients, which makes their jobs even more fulfilling.
In addition to careful client matching, all visits are a minimum of one hour long, so there is plenty of time to provide high quality care and spend time with the client. When you join the Home Instead family you have the best of both worlds – all the benefits of a small, community-based business, but backed with over 25 years of global expertise in providing exceptional home care.

About This Job
Job Purpose / Overview
The Quality Management Lead – Logistics will coordinate the delivery of equipment, materials and documentation across the supply chain, of a major UK infrastructure project, ensuring logistics activities meet project, quality and programme requirements.
The role will act as a key interface between project teams, suppliers, manufacturers, logistics providers and construction teams, overseeing delivery readiness, material traceability, inspection/release and transportation to site.
The QML will act as the single point of contact for supply-chain quality and logistics matters, monitoring supplier performance, supporting inspections, resolving issues and reporting key delivery and quality metrics to ensure Right First Time (RFT) delivery.
The role will also undertake appropriate surveillance of manufacturing documentation and inspections, ensuring equipment is compliant and ready for release and delivery to the construction site.
Key Responsibilities
General
• Support the development of quality (QA/QC) arrangements for deployment across the HPC organisation;
• Implement key quality arrangements related to the following topics:
• Manage Quality Execution
• Support Technical Assessment of Suppliers
• Conducting Manufacturing Surveillance
• Modulating Manufacturing Surveillance
• Management of Non-Conformances
• Quality Release Certificate Process (where applicable)
• Undertake actions to resolve issues relating to the implementation of quality and to bring about improvements, and support others in these actions.
Primary accountability
• Review, accept and monitor Contractors Quality Assurance Plans (CQAP) provided by the supply chain;
• Identify needs for supply chain audits and engage Supply Chain Auditors to perform audits and prompt resolution of findings;
• Produce Project Quality Control Plans (PQCP) for the supply chain;
• In compliance with the PQCP, ensure deployment of key quality contractual arrangements including the General Quality Assurance Specification (GQAS), Life Time Quality Records Specification, Quality Release Certificate and the Inspection & Test Plan Specification etc.
• Provide relevant guidance to contractors, including contractor’s CQAPs, LTQR partitioning strategies and the arrangements for identifying and planning for Quality Related Activities;
• Lead the implementation of LTQR reviews;
• Support the determination and application of strategies for progressive provision of LTQRs by
contractors.
• Develop and maintain effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders including
contracted inspection entities (for offsite manufacturing in particular, Direction Industrielle is a key
stakeholder).
• Ensure manufacturing surveillance per contract is applied in a graded approach of equipment safety function and project importance through surveillance offers and performance monitoring of the inspection agencies used (e.g. Direction Industrielle);
• Ensure overall effectiveness of ITPs submitted by the suppliers, checking that they are fit for purpose from a quality perspective and have been correctly distributed to the relevant internal parties for review and mark-up of the activities they wish to witness;
• Where applicable, establish and check planned inspection witness and hold points marked in the
supplier Inspection and Test Plans (ITP) / Quality Plans / Follow Up Documents (FUDs) and monitor their completion;
• Coordinate, monitor and improve the efficiency of manufacturing documentation review and where applicable, inspection activities performed by contracted inspection entities;
• Coordinate and lead the NNB review and acceptance of relevant manufacturing documentation
provided by contractors;
• Perform joint inspections when required;
• Support the monitoring and technical resolution of non-conformances including the management of corrections and corrective actions;
• Support the review and acceptance of End of Manufacturing Reports (EoMR), End of Construction Status Reports (ECSR) and End of Erection Status Reports (EESR);
• Responsible for the review and delivery of the end of manufacturing records, leading to the quality
release of equipment to the HPC construction site;
• Produce quality documentation (e.g. specifications, procedures) as required.
Secondary accountability
• Implement the quality execution plan within the Programme and undertaken reviews and checks to ensure quality is delivered by the supply chain efficiently and in accordance with programme quality requirements;
• Ensure supplier quality control requirements are adequately specified within contract documentation submitted in the Invitation To Tender (ITT);
• Ensure quality management processes are correctly applied.
Supply Chain & Supplier Management
The post holder will act as a key point of contact for logistics-related matters within their assigned portfolio of suppliers and work packages.
Responsibilities will include:
• Monitoring supplier delivery commitments and recovery plans.
• Challenging suppliers where delivery performance is at risk.
• Coordinating logistics interfaces between multiple suppliers and project functions.
• Tracking equipment status from manufacture through to site delivery.
• Identifying supply-chain constraints and escalating issues appropriately.
• Supporting supplier performance reviews and improvement initiatives.
• Ensuring logistics requirements are clearly understood by suppliers and contractors.
• Maintaining visibility of upcoming deliveries and potential impacts on construction activities.
Logistics Planning & Delivery
The role will support the development and implementation of effective logistics strategies covering:
• Equipment and material delivery planning.
• Shipment and transportation readiness.
• Supplier manufacturing and delivery schedules.
• Inspection and release requirements.
• Material traceability.
• Delivery documentation.
• Site receipt and handover.
• Coordination with construction sequencing and site requirements.
• Management of delivery constraints and programme interfaces.
Reporting & Performance Management
The post holder will provide regular reporting on:
• Supplier delivery performance.
• Equipment/material readiness.
• Upcoming shipments and deliveries.
• Delivery schedule adherence.
• Logistics risks and constraints.
• Outstanding documentation.
• Non-conformances affecting delivery.
• Recovery actions and mitigation plans.
• Key logistics performance indicators.
The role will analyse supply-chain data and provide recommendations to improve delivery performance and mitigate programme risks.
Stakeholder Management
The role requires close collaboration with:
• Programme and Project Management teams.
• Procurement and Commercial functions.
• Engineering and Quality teams.
• Construction and Site teams.
• Equipment manufacturers and suppliers.
• Logistics and transportation providers.
• Inspection organisations.
• Other project delivery functions.
The post holder

About This Job
We are seeking an experienced Permit to Work (PTW) Coordinator / HSE Advisor to join our team at Belfast Dry Dock.
This role is critical in ensuring the safe planning, coordination and execution of high-risk activities within a busy ship repair environment. Acting as the focal point for the site's Permit to Work system, you will ensure work is properly authorised, controlled and monitored while providing practical Health, Safety and Environmental (HSE) support across ship repair, marine and industrial operations.
The successful candidate will be a proactive safety professional with strong permit-to-work experience, excellent communication skills and the confidence to challenge unsafe behaviours where necessary.
Key Responsibilities
Permit to Work Coordination
• Act as the site focal point for the Permit to Work (PTW) system.
• Review, coordinate and issue permits for high-risk activities including:
• Hot Work
• Confined Space Entry
• Working at Height
• Electrical Isolation and Energisation
• Lifting Operations and Crane Activities
• Fuel, Gas and Pressure Systems
• Verify that Risk Assessments and Method Statements (RAMS), isolations and control measures are suitable and sufficient before permits are authorised.
• Ensure permits are correctly briefed, displayed, monitored, closed out and archived.
• Coordinate and manage simultaneous operations (SIMOPS) to prevent conflicting work activities.
• Suspend or withdraw permits where unsafe conditions or non-compliance are identified.
• Support Lock Out / Tag Out (LOTO) processes and verification activities.
HSE Advisory Support
• Provide day-to-day HSE guidance and support to operational teams, contractors and project personnel.
• Ensure compliance with UK and Northern Ireland health and safety legislation, maritime regulations and company procedures.
• Conduct routine workplace inspections, audits and safety tours.
• Support the development and implementation of HSE plans, procedures and safe systems of work.
• Promote a positive safety culture through engagement, coaching and visible leadership.
Contractor & Marine Operations Support
• Support contractor onboarding, inductions and ongoing performance monitoring.
• Ensure contractor compliance with PTW requirements, RAMS and site safety rules.
• Liaise with vessel representatives, supervisors and operational teams regarding work controls and safety arrangements.
• Support safe ship repair, maintenance and marine operations across the site.
Training & Communication
• Deliver PTW briefings, toolbox talks and safety communications.
• Coach permit holders, supervisors and contractors on PTW standards and expectations.
• Encourage reporting of hazards, near misses and unsafe conditions.
• Support workforce engagement initiatives that drive continuous improvement in safety performance.
Reporting & Administration
• Maintain accurate permit registers and HSE records.
• Produce permit-related reports, safety statistics and trend analysis.
• Provide administrative support to the wider HSE function.
• Assist with incident investigations and follow-up actions where required.

Qualifications
Essential Experience & Qualifications
• Recognised Health & Safety qualification.
• Proven experience managing Permit to Work systems within a high-risk environment.
• Experience gained within ship repair, shipbuilding, marine, offshore, heavy engineering or industrial sectors.
• Strong understanding of RAMS, isolations and control of work processes.
• Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
• Ability to challenge unsafe behaviours and maintain safety standards in operational environments.
Desirable
• NEBOSH General Certificate.
• Experience as an Authorised Person.
• Confined Space and/or Hot Work permitting experience.
• Previous experience within dry docks, shipyards, quayside operations or onboard vessels.
• IOSH Membership.
• Knowledge of Lock Out / Tag Out (LOTO) systems.
Key Competencies
• Strong safety leadership skills
• Excellent attention to detail
• Ability to remain firm on safety standards under operational pressure
• Strong planning and coordination abilities
• Practical and solution-focused approach
• Confidence working within live operational and marine environments
• Effective relationship-building and influencing skills

About This Job
We’re looking for an Applied Mathematician or Analytical Physicist with strong analytical instincts, physical intuition and a pragmatic approach to problem-solving to join our Industrials team.
The team develops technologies and products that solve complex real-world challenges across diverse markets, including environmental sensing, semiconductor manufacturing and industrial equipment. Working across multiple disciplines, we combine scientific analysis, physical modelling and engineering to understand problems at a fundamental level and turn that understanding into better products and technologies.
As an Applied Mathematician at TTP, you’ll get to the heart of complex challenges, identify the underlying physical processes and translate them into mathematical models that help guide the way forward. You’ll use first-principles reasoning to challenge assumptions, identify the effects that really matter and make sense of complexity through well-judged simplifications.
The variety is a big part of what makes the role exciting. You could be modelling multiphase flows in complex systems, simulating cutting-edge optoelectronic and photonic technologies, or exploring the feasibility of a novel process and helping guide the scale-up of a prototype design. Each project brings a different challenge, so you’ll need to switch context efficiently, get up to speed quickly in unfamiliar fields and manage several projects in parallel.
Your work will span a broad range of modelling approaches, from analytical calculations and simplified models using MATLAB or custom Python code to detailed numerical simulations, including 3D multiphysics modelling and computational fluid dynamics using tools such as COMSOL. Projects may progress from simple analytical models to more sophisticated simulations.
We value insight and sound judgement as much as analytical rigour. Working at pace, often with incomplete information, you’ll need to know when to investigate further and when a sufficiently good model is enough to make a decision. You’ll also be able to communicate your findings clearly, explaining the implications and uncertainties of your analysis to colleagues and clients, and turning complex results into practical recommendations.
With great facilities, bright and collaborative colleagues and the freedom to innovate, your future at TTP is what you make it. We value ambition, leadership and technical excellence, and provide a fantastic environment in which to develop your career.

Qualifications
We’re looking for an analytical, curious problem-solver who enjoys applying mathematics and physical intuition to complex, real-world challenges.
You’ll ideally bring:
•
A PhD in applied mathematics, physics or a related discipline.
•
Excellent mathematical reasoning, with the ability to translate real-world problems into mathematical models from first principles.
•
Experience developing and using computational models and simulations of physical systems, from simplified analytical approaches to more detailed numerical models.
•
Experience with tools such as MATLAB and/or COMSOL, alongside programming skills in Python or another relevant language to develop your own models and analysis tools.
•
The ability to quickly understand unfamiliar technical problems, identify the key physical processes and adapt your approach across different scientific and engineering domains.
•
A pragmatic approach to analysis, balancing mathematical rigour with the need to reach useful conclusions and make decisions at pace.
•
Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to explain complex analysis clearly and translate results into actionable insights for multidisciplinary teams and clients.

Additional Information
Benefits
TTP is an employee-owned business, based at TTP Campus in Melbourn, just 10 miles south of Cambridge. Our purpose-built, sustainable offices and laboratories are set in green surroundings, creating an inspiring environment for innovation. Our working culture encourages entrepreneurship, shared ideas and technical collaboration, while providing you with the freedom to do your best work.
Our employee benefits include:
• Annual profit-related bonus
• 25 days holiday
• Employer pension contribution of 10% of salary
• Free, nutritious lunch in our on-site restaurant
• Private medical insurance for employees and dependants

Building Inspector - Derby
Are you interested in being a Building Inspector? The tasks you will undertake will include (but are not limited to):
• Conduct comprehensive site inspections and regulatory assessments – Perform building inspections at various construction stages to ensure compliance with Building Regulations, review structural, architectural, and mechanical designs, assess building materials, construction specifications, and fire strategies against relevant Building Regulations and allied legislation
• Supervise inspection activities and enforce regulatory compliance – Act as a Registered Building Inspector within your competency and registered class, supervise lower-class RBIs and graduate trainees, interpret and enforce national and local building regulations (including fire safety, energy efficiency, accessibility, and environmental requirements), and issue formal notices on compliance breaches under the Building Safety Act 2022
• Prepare detailed compliance documentation and provide consultancy services – Produce comprehensive inspection reports, compliance certificates, and regulatory approval documentation, maintain accurate records ensuring traceability and compliance with local authority requirements, and assist clients with Building Regulations consultancy advice where SOCOTEC is not acting as the Registered Building Control Approver

Qualifications
To be a successful  Building Inspector, you should be able to demonstrate:
• Professional qualification and regulatory registration at senior level – Hold membership of RICS, CABE or equivalent (or be qualified by suitable experience), ensure CPD requirements are met to broaden and develop skills, and demonstrate compliance through registration as an RBI at an appropriate level
• Excellent communication and client relationship management skills – Demonstrate strong interpersonal and relationship-building abilities to work effectively with clients and deliver excellent client care across all interactions and project engagements
• Self-starting problem-solver with technical expertise – Show ability to work independently as well as part of large project teams, analyse complex issues, develop suitable solutions, implement these solutions effectively, and keep up to date with changes in building codes, regulations, and industry best practices

Additional Information
Why SOCOTEC?

In this role, you won't just be another employee - you'll be a key player in our continued success story. Your expertise will directly contribute to our mission of building a safer, more sustainable world, while you grow your career alongside some of the industry's finest professionals.

Build a traditional career path or explore opportunities across multiple disciplines - all within SOCOTEC. Your choice, your direction.

Pipeline & Enterprise Revenue Ownership

As the UK’s largest retail, commercial and digital bank, Lloyds Banking Group (LBG) have a big responsibility to support the UK economy and put customers at the heart of everything we do.

About decision science
Sitting within our Risk function, Decision Science is a centre of excellence for analytics, modelling and customer insights. The team support the wider Risk division by:
· Delivering sophisticated data analytics and modelling to support retail and commercial customer needs and credit decisions across the credit lifecycle
· Supporting the bank’s prudential requirements such as capital and impairment allocation, and capital optimisation
We work with data that underpins vital business decisions, and together we make it possible to add customer value, control risk, and help to build a safe, strong bank for our customers.
Our roles are available in a variety of locations, and we support flexible and family-friendly ways of working.
The role of a Senior Analyst - Credit Risk Modelling
Working as part of a team you will support all stages of a prudential model development or maintenance process from understanding the regulations, translating them to an analytical problem statement and experimenting with different modelling approaches to build the most appropriate solution.
As a Senior Analyst in Credit Risk Modelling, you’ll perform the following activities:
•
Develop and maintain prudential capital or impairment models for retail and commercial banking customers · UseSAS (coding language) for data manipulation and analysis
•
Work with Risk and Finance business partners to agree the objectives of analytical projects and ensure they meet regulatory and business requirements
•
Mentoring and coaching of junior colleagues
•
Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams, including internal governance and implementation teams, to deliver effective analytical solutions
The person
We welcome candidates from all personal and career backgrounds and support flexible working arrangements. We'll help you reach your full potential, meet your career aspirations and really make a difference as you embark on a career with excellent development and progression opportunities.
Essential:
•
Minimum of 18 months industry experience delivering predictive analytics in a regulatory or credit risk setting.
•
A strong applied knowledge of statistical modelling e.g. regression or decision trees
•
Proficient in a coding language (e.g. SQL, SAS) to manipulate data and produce insight using predictive analytics techniques. Training and support will be provided for the specific tools required for the role.
•
Ability to present techniques & findings in a clear, visual manner to support senior business partners decision making, including non-technical colleagues.
•
Experience delivering projects as an individual or as part of a wider team.
Desirable:
•
Practical experience in capital or impairment credit-risk modelling techniques and methods is desirable.
•
Prior experience mentoring / coaching junior colleagues is desirable.

•
A competitive salary and annual performance-related bonus
•
A generous annual holiday allowance with the option to purchase up to 5 additional days per year

Private medical insurance

Care Assistant
You think you’re giving a gift… but the biggest surprise? It’s what you get back.
You step into this role thinking you’re there to make someone’s day. And you are.
But here’s what they don’t tell you: the feeling you take home is the real gift.
Picture this:
You visit Mrs. Thompson, who, at 87, still insists on offering you a biscuit with your tea, and pop the kettle on for a good chat. You’re not just helping with her daily routine—you’re the person she looks forward to seeing all week. That conversation? It’s more than just a chat over a cuppa and custard cream. It’s her lifeline. Your hourly visits are the one thing she relies on to get through the week, the support she knows will always be there when the world feels a little too quiet.
And then there’s Mr. Harris. You help him lace up his boots, take his hand, and guide him on his favourite winter walk along Kemble High Street. You walk side by side, his dog trotting along, and it feels simple — just another part of your day. But when he looks at you and smiles, “I couldn’t do this without you,” you feel the weight of those words. What you thought was just a walk? It’s his independence. It’s his connection to a world that would be out of reach without you.
And at the end of the day?
You go home, wrap your hands around a hot chocolate, and that feeling stays with you. It’s not just ticking off a list—it’s knowing you’ve actually made a difference in someone’s day. That’s the kind of fulfilment that’s hard to find anywhere else. You’ll find it with us, at Home Instead.
Whether you’ve worked in care before or it’s your first time, we provide all the training and support you need so you can feel confident and capable from day one. You’ll never feel alone—we’re here to support you in everything you do.
We’re looking for people who are naturally caring, curious about the stories our clients have to share, and passionate about learning new skills. Many of our Care Professionals have never worked in care before, but they all share that one thing in common: a heart for helping others.
And we make sure you’re well looked after, too. With pay rates up to £15 an hour and all visits lasting at least one hour, you’ll have the time to truly get to know each client—without feeling rushed. We are rated GOOD by the Care Quality Commission.

If you’re looking for a role where the biggest reward is more than a pay slip, and you want to go home knowing you’ve made a difference, we’d love to hear from you.

• Analysing and implementing the latest techniques and advances.
• Generating novel concepts and approaches.
• Researching potential vulnerabilities, often for niche applications.
• Rapid prototyping and troubleshooting.
• Designing and implementing proof-of-concept demonstrators.
• Analysing results and drawing and presenting conclusions.
• Making recommendations for further research.
Projects will also stretch and develop your commercial awareness, through partnership with clients to understand their needs and deliver high-quality outcomes at pace.

Qualifications
Person Specification
Successful applicants will demonstrate some of the following key attributes:
• Hold a strong undergraduate degree in a relevant subject including (but not limited to) Maths, Physics, Engineering, or Computer Science.
• Demonstrate applied experience in vulnerability research.
• Be a fluent programmer in C, C++ or Python.
• Possess knowledge of how system software and hardware interact at a low-level, for example, at the operating system driver level.
• Bring an outside-the-box approach, creative problem-solving ability, independent mindset, and broad interest in developments across cyber security.
• Be able to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing.
• Possess the ability to work both autonomously and collaboratively within an expert team in a high-performing environment.
The following are desirable but not essential:
• Experience in the UK Defence and Security sector.
• Experience of, or the skills required for, client-facing roles.
• Technical expertise in one or more of the following areas:
• Reverse engineering.
• Cyber-physical systems.
• Network and protocol analysis.
• Low-level programming on embedded systems or similar.
• Virtualisation and containerisation.
• Simulation, modelling and data analysis.
Owing to the fast-paced, collaborative nature of our work, successful applicant(s) would be expected to work full time on-site, in our state-of-the-art office and labs at the TTP Campus (Cambridge Road, Melbourn, SG8 6HQ).

Additional Information
Why Awerian?
Awerian is a research and technology development consultancy, comprising ~40 mathematicians, scientists, and engineers. Awerian provides advanced R&D services to the UK defence and national security sector and specialises in delivering innovative solutions at pace to its clients’ most challenging technical problems. As part of the wider TTP Group, Awerian works closely with its sister consultancy TTP plc and shares state-of-the-art facilities within a purpose-built campus in green surroundings close to Cambridge.

About This Job
As a financial technology company moving billions of GBP of customer money in over 70 countries, Wise must have bulletproof financials. We need timely, accurate, and scalable financial data to be compliant with regulations and make strategic business decisions to support our hyper-growth and financial objectives.
Due to our continued expansion, we’re on the hunt for a seasoned, highly strategic Finance Business Partner Leader to join our FP&A team in London. In this role, you will be the primary lead for the financial oversight of our Core Functions, responsible for mentoring and developing a high-performing group of two Senior Finance Business Partners and an Analyst. Your core focus will be supervising team output and leaning into complex business challenges, while spearheading our global workforce financial strategy and collaborating cross-functionally with peer FBPs Leads.
Your Mission
You will be the ultimate strategic financial partner to our Chief People Officer (CPO), her People Leadership Team and the Senior Leadership Teams that lead our Core Functions (Finance, Legal, Treasury, Risk, Compliance, and People). In addition to managing costs within the Functions, your mission will be to help us centralise and actively optimise how we manage workforce costs by improving our internal processes, driving strategic location expansion and extending our planning horizon.
Key Responsibilities
•
Leadership & Team Management: Lead , mentor, and elevate two Senior Finance Business Partners and Analyst, ensuring cohesive delivery of financial planning, cost control, and analysis across all Functions.
•
Executive Narrative & Communication: Translate complex financial data and variance analyses into high-impact strategic narratives for the leadership team, providing actionable insights that influence company-wide decision-making.
•
KPI-driven Performance Management: Establish, track, and own the critical financial KPIs and metrics relating to organisational health, span of control, location concentration, and cost-per-head to drive accountability across departments
•
Global Headcount Governance: Oversee employee benefit expenses and headcount management framework for the entire business. You will collaborate closely with stakeholders and peer Senior FBPs across other departments to ensure a unified, standardised approach to headcount management.
•
Automation & Process Evolution: Drive  the automation of headcount tracking and employee benefit expenses reporting towards scalable, tool-driven architectures to maximise efficiency and data integrity.
•
Strategic Workforce Management: Partner with the CPO and People Leadership Team to drive the long-term financial strategy behind global workforce location expansion, talent mapping, and organisation design to optimize our workforce costs sustainably.
This role will give you the opportunity to:
•
Lead and Scale a Team: Act as a player-coach, mentoring senior talent within your team while building strong connections across the wider FP&A team and beyond
•
Shape Global Strategy: Play a defining role in how Wise scales its global footprint and optimises its largest investment our people through progressive, long-term workforce planning.
•
Drive Executive Level Influence: Act as a trusted advisor to the leadership team, turning complex data into clear, actionable insights that guide our global investment decisions.

Qualifications
A bit about you:
•
People Management & Collaboration: Proven track record of managing senior-level finance professionals and driving matrixed collaboration with peer finance partners to achieve company-wide objectives.
•
Deep Strategic Partnering: Extensive proven experience partnering with senior leadership teams, specifically within People and Functions, becoming a deeply trusted advisor.
•
Workforce & Scale Expertise: Demonstrated track record of managing complex, company-wide headcount structures, long-term workforce planning, international location strategies, and substantial operational expense budgets.
•
Data & Automation Mindset: Passionate about leveraging technology and automation to eliminate manual processes; strong experience building KPI dashboards and predictive models.
•
Financial Modelling Mastery: Advanced expertise in building, scaling, and owning complex financial frameworks and capacity models, with a strong preference for enterprise planning tools (e.g., Anaplan).
•
Credentials: You hold a professional finance qualification (ACA / ACCA / CIMA) or equivalent (MBA / Masters in Finance) with extensive post-qualification experience, alongside a strong grasp of IFRS and corporate accounting.
Skills:
•
High-Level Influencer: Exceptional communication skills with the ability to articulate complex financial concepts clearly and strategically to influence the leadership team.
•
Systemic Thinker: You love digging into data, but you naturally zoom out to see the macroeconomic and organisational interdependencies, applying a strict KPI-driven lens to problem-solving.
•
Comfortable with Ambiguity: Highly adaptable, resilient, and thrives in a fast-paced, evolving tech environment. Firm and forceful on guardrails when required, yet collaborative.
•
Project Leadership: Strong project management skills, capable of driving cross-functional alignment across multiple offices, time zones, and complex stakeholder groups.
•
Humble Execution: While you operate at a leadership level, you aren't afraid to roll up your sleeves and validate the data yourself when needed.
Bonus points for:
•
Experience in a hyper-growth FinTech or fast-paced global tech company.
•
Direct experience working closely with Workday and Anaplan integrations.
•
A background utilising AI to optimise financial processes, data pipelines, and headcount forecasting.

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/williamsracing/.description_excerpt:
About This Job
Most digital design manager roles ask you to maintain what’s already been built. This one asks you to raise it. Williams F1 Team is in the middle of a serious brand evolution, and digital is the primary surface where fans, partners and the wider world experience it. The website, the app, the campaigns around the season’s biggest moments — these are where the brand lives in real time, and right now they have room to be significantly better. You’ll lead the digital creative output, owning the quality and direction of everything we put into the world across our owned digital channels. You’ll sit at the intersection of creative, social and brand — working directly with the Head of Creative, Head of Social and Head of Brand to make sure the digital work is integrated, consistent and genuinely excellent. This is a leadership role that carries real creative accountability, not just a coordination function. If you’re a senior designer ready to step up and run something, or a design manager who wants to do the best work of your career inside a genuinely iconic sport, this is the role.
Lead the Digital Creative
• Own the creative direction and quality bar across all digital outputs — williamsf1.com, the Williams F1 Team app, campaign assets, email, and the digital moments around key race activations.
• Set the standard for how the Williams brand expresses itself digitally, pushing the work to be sharper, more distinctive and more effective over time.
• Lead concept development for the season’s biggest digital moments — race activations, livery reveals, fan campaigns and product launches — from brief through to delivery.
• Oversee and contribute hands on to design work across the team, maintaining quality without becoming a bottleneck.
Integrate Across Creative, Social and Brand
• Work directly and regularly with the Head of Creative, Head of Social and Head of Brand to align digital creative with the broader brand and content strategy.
• Ensure digital outputs are genuinely integrated with social campaigns and brand activity — not treated as a separate stream.
• Act as the connective tissue between teams, spotting where creative could be unified and making it happen.
• Bring a point of view into senior creative conversations — representing the digital channel with authority and advocating for its potential.
Drive Performance and Fan Growth
• Partner with the Fan Growth & Performance team to deliver creative that performs — high quality assets built for paid and organic channels, optimised for reach, engagement and conversion.
• Champion a test and learn culture across digital creative — building systems and templates that allow for rapid iteration without sacrificing craft.
• Use performance data and fan insight to inform creative decisions and push for the next iteration of the work.
• Support the development of scalable creative systems that serve both the always on programme and campaign moments.
Build and Develop the Team
• Manage, mentor and develop the digital design team, creating an environment where craft is taken seriously and people grow.
• Lead briefing, feedback and review processes so the team has clarity and direction without being micromanaged.
• Identify resourcing needs, manage external partners and help shape the structure of the team as the function matures.
• Set a culture of accountability, creative ambition and collaborative working.
Evolve the Digital Design System
• Own the digital component library, design system and motion principles, keeping them current and genuinely useful to the people building with them.
• Work with the Head of Brand to ensure digital outputs are consistent with and actively strengthening the wider visual identity.
• Identify where the brand could be doing more digitally — more confident, more distinctive, more fan facing — and make the case for it.

Qualifications
• 7 or more years of design experience, with a proven track record leading digital creative at a senior level — ideally inside a fast moving consumer, sports or entertainment brand, or a top agency working in that space.
• A strong creative leader with a clear point of view and the credibility to bring others with you — whether that’s a junior designer, a head of social or a senior stakeholder.
• Deeply fluent across the full digital canvas: web, app, campaign, performance creative, brand. You understand how each surface works and what excellent looks like on each one.
• Experienced managing and developing designers, with a genuine interest in building a team and not just doing the work yourself.
• Highly collaborative and comfortable operating at the intersection of multiple creative disciplines — you’ve worked closely with social, brand and marketing leads before and you know how to make integrated creative happen.
• Expert in Figma and Adobe Creative Suite (Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, After Effects). You can get in the tools when the work demands it.
• Data informed but creatively led — you understand how to use performance insight to improve the work without letting it flatten it.
• Calm under pressure, decisive when it counts, and genuinely collaborative with the people around you.
• Passionate about Formula 1 — or the kind of person who commits fully to whatever sport or culture they get close to.
• Degree in Graphic Design, Digital Media or a related field preferred; exceptional portfolio over credentials.

Additional Information
Atlassian Williams F1 Team is an equal opportunity employer that values diversity and inclusion. We are happy to discuss reasonable job adjustments.

About This Job
About the role:
Engineering Experience looks after developer productivity at Wise. We work in two ways. We operate services that engineers rely on every day, and we are the pillar team responsible for improving engineering productivity across Wise.
We are looking for an experienced software engineer who wants to make life better for other engineers. You will build and run tools, help set our technical direction and work directly with teams so the things we create are useful in practice. This is a hands-on role for someone who writes strong production software and is comfortable teaching, advocating and leading change.
How we work:
Everything we build needs to work for more than 1,200 engineers. That scale matters. We are not looking for isolated wins. Saving every engineer an hour has a huge impact, so we focus on common problems and solutions that work across Wise.
We learn by talking to engineers, looking at usage data and seeing how our services behave in production. We use that evidence to design, build and operate improvements that are secure, reliable and easy to use. Adoption is part of the engineering work. We run workshops, write practical guidance and communicate in large engineering forums to help good tools become everyday habits.
We are an AI first team using agentic development tools across the entire SDLC to enhance our productivity and have more impact at Wise. We do not use the tools to replace what we care about, which is people, relationships and working as a team.
What will you be working on?:
•
Owning and operating the agentic tooling used by engineers across Wise, including security, access to models and tools, telemetry and evaluation.
•
Building an engineering knowledge base exposed through a MCP server, so engineers and AI agents can find trusted internal context when they need it.
•
Leading AI enablement across engineering through hands-on workshops, practical guidance and adoption campaigns that help teams use these tools confidently in their day-to-day work.
•
Building and operating products that remove friction across software development, from local setup and code review through to deployment and operation.
•
Improving the developer portal and other shared engineering services so tools, guidance and engineering signals are easy to find and act on.
•
Using research, feedback and data to find problems shared by many teams, then turning them into software and changes that save engineers time across Wise.
What do you need?:
•
A senior engineer comfortable working in a polyglot environment. Our tools and services span languages including Java, Go, Python and TypeScript. You need to be an expert in either Java, Go or TypeScript, but not all of them.
•

About This Job
Environmental Health Technician
Full-time
We need every soldier and officer to be fit and well, so that we have an active, capable Army. That means protecting our troops’ health and wellbeing, wherever they are in the world. As an Environmental Health Technician, you advise commanders on environmental health, occupational hygiene, preventing disease and environmental protection. Whenever troops are deployed, you go out beforehand on reconnaissance missions to check out the location and risks. It’s important work – but don’t worry – you’ll get the highest standard of training.
Find where you belong.
WORLD-CLASS TRAINING
If you want to be an Environmental Health Technician, you'll start with your initial military training which will teach you how to be a soldier - this will cover everything from fieldcraft to how to handle a rifle. Your initial training will be at either Pirbright or Winchester and last for 14 weeks.
Then you’ll begin practical training at the Defence School of Healthcare Education. At the same time, you’ll do a BSc (Hons) degree in Environmental Health from Leeds Beckett University. You will gain a NEBOSH General Certificate in Occupational Health and a BPCA Certificate in Pest Control over three years.
GAIN QUALIFICATIONS
All Environmental Health Technicians can gain postgraduate qualification throughout their career and you may also have the opportunity to study at MSc level.
SHOW PEOPLE WHAT YOU’RE CAPABLE OF
We'll be with you every step of the way as you move up the ranks. From the moment you begin your training you'll get all the support and encouragement you need to make a success of your career. Work hard and you'll soon get promoted, which means more responsibility and extra pay.
Become an Environmental Health Technician and you’ll:
-           Earn £15,671 during training. When your training is finished, and you join your Unit, pay will rise to £21,600.
-           Receive subsidised accommodation and facilities, increasing your disposable income
-           Receive free medical and dental health cover
-           Have the continuous access promotional opportunity and to continually progress your career
-           Be sponsored to earn valuable civilian-recognised qualifications
-           Take part in Adventurous Training and be able to play your favourite sports.
BELONG TO SOMETHING THAT MATTERS.
You should be:
• Regular Army age: 16.6 – 35.6 years
• Army Reserve age:
New enlistments: 17.9 – 43 years
Ex-Regular: 17.9 – 52 years
Specialist (Soldier): 17.9 – 50 years
Qualifications you’ll need:
104 UCAS points from 2 A Levels or equivalent, excluding General Studies. GCSE Grade A–C/9-4 in at least English Language, Maths and two sciences. For full entry criteria information, please visit the Leeds Beckett University Website
Fitness requirements:
• Mid Thigh Pull 46kg
• Medicine Ball Throw 2.9m
• 2km run 11m 15s (11m30s for Junior Entry)
Our next deadline for application is 31st March 2023, with further opportunities ongoing throughout the year.

​You will join our UK Water team as an experienced hydrologist and hydraulic modeller, bringing strong technical expertise and relevant consultancy or industry experience. You will apply your knowledge of hydrology, hydraulic modelling and flood risk assessment across a varied portfolio of projects. Our work ranges from UK infrastructure and development schemes to major international assignments involving climate resilience, water management, mining, hydropower and technical due diligence. • Strong Commercial focus.

• Ability to identify new sales and revenue opportunities.

• Ability to influence at all levels.
• Enthusiastic team player.

Insight and analytical skills

Knowledge

Skills and approach

Overview
Shape the future of regulatory monitoring in the water industry.
The water industry is facing increasing scrutiny and investment in environmental performance, wastewater monitoring and regulatory compliance. Reliable reporting depends not only on data, but on the instrumentation, operational practices and management systems behind it.
We are looking for a Regulatory Monitoring Consultant to join our Asset and Information Management practice and help grow our specialist capability.
Working alongside our Technical Authority for Regulatory Monitoring and Compliance and a wider multidisciplinary team, you will help water companies manage monitoring risk from sensor to submission and beyond.

Your work will vary across client assignments and may include:
• Analysing wastewater flow, spill, process and instrumentation data to identify anomalies, trends and potential compliance risks.
• Supporting flow-compliance investigations, root-cause analysis and corrective-action planning.

• Assessing whether monitoring arrangements and available data are fit for their intended operational and regulatory purpose.
• Supporting the development and assessment of instrumentation, quality or environmental management systems.
